segments.summary: In July 2026, the ICF welcomed 21 new members, driven by credentialing interest, heat-wave cave management resources, and last-minute registrations for the Annual Conference in Madison. Of the 25 renewals due, 19 renewed—highlighted by Binta Krueger upgrading to SmallBusiness—while 6 low-engagement members lapsed, keeping retention aligned with the 2026 stabilization baseline. Event bookings were strong, with 128 late registrations bringing the Madison conference to 383 total attendees despite summer heat advisories, and 255 new bookings for the Bega food safety workshop.

segments.summary: In August 2026, the ICF welcomed 77 new members (42 Individual, 19 Enthusiast, 13 SmallBusiness, and 3 Corporate), closely tracking last year's volume as fall onboarding for the Cheese Foundations Certificate, cross-border tariff guidance, and federal traceability rule advocacy drove steady sign-ups. Out of 69 due renewals, 58 renewed (an 84.1% retention rate), including upgrades by Ashley Delacroix to SmallBusiness and Stefan Mikkelsen to Corporate, while 11 low-engagement first-year members lapsed and 4 late-month invoices remained unpaid at window close. Early registration opened for the October Curd Food Safety workshop in Boise with 8 bookings, slightly ahead of typical lead times following the federation's late-August Listeria swab-mapping webinar promo.
